title: The Gilbert–Pollak Steiner-ratio conjecture
formal: For every finite set of at least two points in the Euclidean plane, is the length of its minimum spanning tree at most 2/√3 times the length of its Euclidean Steiner minimal tree?
context:
Historical claimed proofs had gaps. Euclidean length and unrestricted Steiner points are essential.

This question was found through Wikipedia and compared individually with the existing candidate and archived records. The linked literature provides definitions and background; this import is not a completed research-card review.
why: Would identify the exact worst-case saving obtained by adding junctions to a geometric network.
